A bit off topic...but have been trying to determine which argument regarding butter vs margarine makes the most sense. There are still very rationale, very well sourced arguments on both sides. Wanted to know how this group weighs in on the discussion and if you have any good readings on it.
Butter, what is natural can not be all that bad for me & mine.

Butter has better supplies of Calcium and Potassium. Butter has more saturated fat, while Margarine is mostly unsaturated fats (more monounsaturated than polyunsaturated) and five times the Trans Fats. That said, from a fat standpoint Margarine has healthier fats, even with the trans fats considered. Butter wins in micronutrient content though.

Margarine also has less cholesterols, especially LDL cholestorols which is a good thing.

In the end though, neither should be used in large quantities, so It's a moot point if they're used sparingly. By Sparingly I mean not going all Paula Deen and butter-frying butter breaded butter in a butter based butter hollandise butter sauce. :)
